tone | maybe fallout has a better atmosphere but i might be shaded by nostalgia in that aspect plust i have to applaud f:nv doing post-apocolypse in a different way | where fallout is a game about people surviving out of a destroyed and fractured world | fallout: new vegas is about people living in rebuilt societies after the descrution of social systems | in fallout people were fighting for resources more aside from the two mega-factions of the brotherhood of steel and the enclave | in f:nv enter even more factions all with conflicting ideologies | you play as a more or less fish out of water protagonist forced to interact with these extant social groups and have the unique ability due to circumstance to change the balance of power in the region | how so and how much is all left up to you | while i lament that you can't play after the game's ending i | e | you have to revert to a previous save this is probably one of the best video game endings created for a game so focused on player choice mass effect take note | your actions can have forseeable and unforseeable consequences to the different groups you come into contact with that all tie together in not a necessarily happy way but a very satisfying way | there are oodles of quests to do and you won't probably find everything in one playthrough | it wasn't till my rd playthrough till i found a npc follower that i've never met before with a fully fleshed character and a emotionally resonant side quest | there is just so many stories to uncover in this game which would be difficult to find in just one playthrough if you aren't using guides | the gameplay is more polished than fallout allowing for iron sights toggleable and way way more weapons | there are more healing options more chem buffs and new craftable items to aid you in a scrape but there is also more balance in using these items since all healing items besides stimpacks heal over time | long gone are the days of spamming nuka-colas to heal tacked on system but once i started using it i saw how wrong i was | using different ammo types really allow you to get the most potential out of your guns and should never be underused | i have to admit the engine to this game isn't great or stable which kind of gives combat a bit of wonkeyness and less impact as is the same of fallout but that kind of wonkeyness is almost endearing | and like any bethesda title this game has a prolifiic modding scene from graphical enhancements engine enhancements more raido tracks rebuiltrebalanced game systems new game locations new types of gameplay new followers and quests or just plain weird stuff that are all relatively easy to install thanks to the game's own mod api and nexus mod client and other various mod clients like boss | finally the dlc in the beginning even minor enemies will kick your butt | but as you learn the weaknesses of dozens of unique enemiy types from the bestiary craft equipment and learn to anticipate their attack patterns it feels like you're becoming a master monster hunter by your own efforts | the combat is also difficult enough that you can never button mash your way through it even on the easiest difficulty settings | and if you know what you are doing and have a lot of patience you can take on foes of much higher level then yourself | combat is frantic and methodical at the same time | i love it | the game also understands the importance of context: almost all contracts missions and game mechanics feel like they take place in a world where they make sense | every character is fully voiced every quest has a dramatic arc | it really feels like your actions matter | the witcher is also a technical marvel able to load huge maps quickly and seemlessly while maintaining dynamic weather and gorgeous facial animation | there are a few glitches but they are hardly noticable compared to those of other games of this scope | all in all it seems like cd projekt red have poured a lot of love compares to this experience | i truly feel without any hyperbole that this game was the best game i have ever played | rpgs are tricky beasts | you want a lot of engaging content but that means you need to fill that content out thoroughly | usually even the best games of the genre have this quasi three-tier system to their content: the main story the secondary stuff and the tertiary random filler | the first of the three usually has well thought out well scripted well voiced content thats fully engaging and advances the story | the second usually is a little less on those marks but still of an okay quality and sometimes affects the story as an option | lastly the third is basically quickie throw away go fetch me x number of y content sometimes without even vo and interactions | with this game however its more like a two-tier system with the second tier only barely sitting below the first | even the most fluff of fluffy filler content felt compelling engaging fun and i had to played over hours of this game almost solely in the domain of velen and so much of that has been off the beaten track | the various points of interest are always intriguing to discover and that is no mean feat | you could find yourselves doing anything from liberating a small village from a camp of bandits to chasing after legendary witcher gear across the breadth of the continent | geralt of rivia is a monster hunter a sword for hire and the game really shines through with its investigation mechanics | when you go on a monster hunt you are expected to use all of geralt's heightened witcher senses to track the beast to its lair or to lure it out into the open | this mechanic and the way in which it is used adds variety to the questing and gives you the chance to immerse yourself review_text: now that the game is finished after some hours i must confess i was skeptical throughout the development process thinking that cdpr could not deliver what they promised | after the credits rolled i knew i was right to that scepticism but still cdpr managed to delivered where mattered the most | people may come to this believing this is the next skyrim or dark souls and they might be disappointed when they realise the wild hunt is the next witcher game and this is a beast on its own | the 'open world' claim is kind of misleading the game features some huge areas to roam but still there are borders and forced transitions between them | still the world feels lived in and is beautiful | the vistas are breathtaking the villages and cities feel alive and i was literally holding my breath when i saw my first sunset outside white orchad as well as some otherworldly places during act | the monster and character design is also great and the graphics are awesome even on a so-so rig mine was able to run the game at high settings with fps but the end result was worth it even though it took quite a toll on my pc towards the end the witcher games are first and foremost story-based games and this one is no exception | the story starts really slow with a gentle whimper as you get accustomed to the world and the gameplay | it really starts to pick up though after you get to the main area story quests especially the red baron one and hold until act | there i felt as if the open world structure failed to convey the urgency and momentum of the story as it was done in the final acts of the first witcher for instance or perhaps they were rushed to get to the shipping date | still though there are plenty of chills and thrills and some nice twists to the story | the writing is once more superb and there are moments you will laugh and moments you will cry moments you will love the characters and moments you will hate them | the dialogues are top notch and the characters greatly written | what really sets apart the wild hunt from most contemporary wrpgs and sets a high bar for the next wave of similar titles is the quest structure | it is really impressive how the relatively short side-quests are so rich in story ambience details and are in themselves self-contained stories | often i would return from work and turn on the game to play a couple of them to unwind as if i was watching episodes from a tv series | and most impressive few of them feel like fodder to pad up the game but they feel organic and tie quite well to the themes of the game | that is quite the feat | choices | choices | this is what the witcher games are reknowned for the choices and their concequences | we were promised that all our choices mattered and in the end they do not that much: no matter what you did last two game the world is the same and only some events reflect them | i don't think there is a choice that will change the way you play the quest just some quests are altered based on your choices | it may be cdpr ditching some of their most ambitious plans for practical reasons or as a statement that geralt even though a skilled individual thrown in the thick of things he cannot affect any real change | or when watching how different choices lead to some very narrow consequence branches or no branches at all at the powerlessness of a man or the power of destiny or cdpr not going towards a fully every-choice-really-matters path still some of the consequences come to haunt you hours latter good deeds are rewarded or punished | what really stands out though is that many choices have little affect on chats andor rewards and how irrationalemotionally invested some of the choices can be | there were times i had to read all the answers many times wondering what i should do and times i would intentionally do something non-heroic when considering my past actions as geralt | it might sound as a criticism but truth is i am more than happy with the way the choice system works and in the end it is years ahead from competition | combat is initially nothing to write home about | it is more streamlined compared to w and there are difficulty levels to keep anyone but the most hardcore soul fans happy | it is obviously a game meant to be played by everybody as it should | then as you get your hands on new skills better equipment and more potions it really hits home how great is the battle | geralt is supposed to be a genetically engineered killing machine and he is the butcher of blavitken those familiar with the source material remember he offed a band of notorious mercenaries within seconds and plays exactly like that | the controlls are fluid and the battle really feels great when you get the hang of it | true you can spam quen and fast attack and even slog through the death march difficulty but what makes the combat really stand out is finding that one tactic that turns that dreaded boss battle into a literal cakewalk | which brings me to my main criticism towards all three witcher games: as soon as you explore get good equipment and level up the difficulty goes out of the window | still the story and the feel of the game will hold you some more | i've mentioned the source material and during the last two games there was criticism about the disparity between geralt in the game and geralt from the books | i think this one is much more respectful to sapowski's novels right down to some post-modern ideas used in the plot for instance ciri the damsel in distress can in fact hold on her own and leaves geralt do some of her dirty work | there has also been quite some criticism about sexism in the previous games and i felt that this time cdpr addressed much of those criticism by adding some really quests about strong women trying to find their place in a man's world | what really stands out to me though is the grimness of the world | this is not a dark world far from it | it is colourfull and full of life and joy as it is full with horrors and attrocity | what really makes the witcher such a dark game is the fact that nobody moans and es about injustices | there are no montages of soldiers and dramatic music scores or characters telling their sob stories yes da i am talking about you | instead everyone is treating war death pestilence racism and prejudice as if it is the norm a very eastern european mentallity that gives the game a unique feel to it and makes small acts of kindness feel like epic feats | geralt may concert with kings and witches but at the end of the day he is protecting the simple man from monsters with both steel and silver swords and the game never loses sight of this | major props to the excelent sound design and the great and atmospheric music | overall an rpg worth playing my personal game of the ploughing year ploughing

review_text: very few games move me enough to have me consider a second play through | bioshock infinite is one of those games | from the story to the combat i have enjoyed every last second of the columbia experience | please don't compare this to previous games with similar titles | and as such i will not compare them in this recommendation | what i will do is explain what i love about infinite and if it jives with what you also love in games then you will enjoy this experience as well | for one without any spoilers the story is tremendous | not dickens or shakespeare but for sci-fi fans who enjoy stories that try to stretch the imagination this definitely satisfies | columbia itself is nicely fleshed-out with a lot of details | it's nice to see a city that is seemingly pleasant until you see the underlying fanaticism and bigotry | it is almost uncomfortable and off-putting but makes the experience that much more real | besides story and setting the remaining piece would be combat of which i found quite satisfying | if you're not a fan of bullet-spongy baddies you've definitely come to the wrong place | i played through on hard the first time and the game definitely gave me a challenge | with only two weapons to swap between and a limited amount of salt for vigors read plasmids i had to be very careful | it was easy to get myself killed by running out into the open; interesting characters at least the ones of any significance to the story | without spoiling too much the high point of the story is definitely the confrontation at the end between clay and the villain; it is realistically one of my favorite moments in any video game | the story isn't perfect it isn't as good as mafia ii's story and is sadly spread too far and few between by an abundance of repetitive and unskippable story missions that don't actually progress the plot | overall though the story and characters are so well written that it has to be a plus | combat: combat is definitely improved in this game over its predecessors | the inclusion of the stealth and brutal execution mechanics are key points which make this a fun game to play | nothing is more satisfying than brutally stabbing a mafiosa repeatedly in the face and then taking out his startled friend with a close range shotgun to the gut that sends him ragdolling back through the air | there is also a great amount of flexibility in the combat tactics you can use in the game | stealth going in guns-a-blazing and any mixture of the two are all valid and useable combat tactics in mafia iii | it also is really rewarding to stealth through one of the racket missions just to sneak up on the man in charge and grab him before he knows what's going on | i do need to make note that the ai is pretty stupid especialy when it comes to the stealth; they will often times look right past you and you can make them throw caution to the wind with a simple whistle to draw them to an area where you can stealth kill them with a simple press of the 'q' key | the flexibility doesn't just come in tactics either | there are a wide range of weapons and explosives to choose from | although it is kind of lame that you have very limited ammo supplies even with the upgrades and additionally can only carry two weapons one small arms and one large arms weapon | i found myself often times dropping the extremely overpriced weapons i had bought purely out of the lack of ammo supply | regardless of these small issues the combat definitely felt improved over mafia ii | exploration: exploring new bordeaux in mafia iii is a lot of fun | each area feels pretty different from any of the others which is crazy considering there are different areas in the city | while exploration isn't very fruitful aside from gathering collectibles see cons it is still enjoyable for explorations sake | if you want to be rewarded tangibly for exploring you may not enjoy the exploration but if you just enjoy virtual site seeing you'll have a good time | soundtrack: the soundtrack is great | while i prefered mafia ii's soundtrack jazz is my jam the use of classic rock songs at specific points of the game was great | be effective | similarly the armor that you spent $ on would disappear after a shotgun shot and pistol shot combined | while it may be helpful in a few situations on the whole it doesn't really do too review_text: mafia iii the follow up to the legendary mafia and mafia ii video games | i was very hyped for this game and was anticipating an epic game much like grand theft auto v | however there are a few things that make gameplay a less enjoyable experience | let me start off by saying the story is excellent and while i haven't played through the entire game yet i will hopefully change this review by the end of all the dlcs and updates | the story is very engaging and unique | there are also plenty of elements that reinforce the notion of racism during this period: such as when police respond slower and the dispatcher uses words like 'maybe' in poorer black neighborhoods | however story aside the game is hard to love when the physics and graphics are sub-par | while the game does look pretty at times there are some glaring details i cannot forgive | the first thing you'll notice is that the graphics are wonky at times | the lighting and reflections and wonky and the chrome on the cars looks more like matte plastic with a metallic paint | sometimes the immediate world also darkens and lightens as if the developers wanted to emulate clouds obscuring the sun intermittently but it comes across as jarring | at night new bordeaux looks very beautiful though | i think the developer added too many post-process effects that take away from the performance this should be looked into but i think the only way to fix this is to redo the entire game engine | as mentioned the physics and overall feel of the game is lacking | driving feels like the cars are driving with ice wheels | while yes older american cars had wonky and floaty suspensions and the game allows them to leans as such the wheels are like they are made of ice and the cars feel lighter than they look | the physical damage on cars is also dissapointing as i was looking up to gta v and taking cues from older movies where the sheet metal cars would actually tear themselves apart after a collision | colliding with people also seems like an unfinished feature | i feel the devs would have had a better time if they used natural motion as the people are more like lamp posts with animations coming in late | sometimes the ai driven cars have erratic driving that is pretty annoying to deal with: they would be spinning around in an 's' shape right in front of me and would clip through other cars until they are right in front of me where the game engine decides that they should have collision again | another point of contention is general gameplay | i'm currently in the stage where i'm running introductory jobs for cassandra vito and burke | but all of these characters have had the same type of missions to regain control of their respective territories: go there bop that guy until the big boss guy gets anfry and shows his face go back to the same large wardehouse place you bopped one guy to get the big guy finished | as stated i haven't finished the main story yet but i hope the missions are not going to be monogamous for the rest of the crew again | tldr; well told story everything else is sub-par | get this game on sale or a few years down the line |

review_text: edit: i just beat the game so i decided to reformat the review and add any final thoughts i never got around to playing mafia but i loved everything about mafia back in the day | the gritty realism the somewhat unique story and all the small mechanics that made the world feel so real and different from the other sandbox games at the time | if i had to choose right now i would probably play it over gta | because of this i got relatively excited for this iteration | i avoided every trailer gameplay video and blog post to not get my hopes up so that i could have an ubiased and uninformed play through this game | but after only a day of playing i have realized that this is a poor mans gta for a rich mans price | pros: story: the beginning ending and some of the story missions in between are very well done and will motivate some people to get through the repetitiveness of the game setting: i don't remember any games that take place in the racist south during the s playing as a black man on top of that just sweatens the deal soundtrack: every time i play a game like fallout mafia or gta i love the soundtrack | this game is no different | however it is a let down that there are only three radio stations to choose from characters: the personality for each main and side character is unique and very well done | and their voice acting is top notch | i wasn't suprised to see the long list of voice actors in the credits because no one sounds identical cutscenes: every time a cutscene starts i have to sit back and just appreciate how good they look | other than some small shadow and clipping issues the character models and facial animations are amazingly done | however this is also a negative because once you get back into the game it brings home how ugly it is story missions: the only interesting and unique missions are the story missions which take place after taking over a district | there are around of these missions not all of them are good with boring filler missions in between each one cons: graphics: this game is ugly | the intro cutscene got me excited to delve into a nice looking game but it is obvious that this is a console port once you actually start playing | it's almost comparable to a mid gen ps game | where are the gta level graphics that are shown in the cutscenes | i found that the only time this game looks good is at very specific times of the day and at night | for about % of the day the sun is blindingly bright and washes everything out pop in: this ties into the graphics | cars and objects pop into view about yards ahead of you which makes driving really fast in the oncoming lane very dangerous | the pop in is even more evident in the rearview mirror | a wall of brown chases you and swallows everything yards behind you audio: everything is cranked up to the max | no matter how far away someone is yelling from you it sounds like they are right next to you | this makes it very difficult to track down the last guy you have to kill driving: i don't even know what happened here | i've tried both driving modes and simulation mode is the most playable but they both feel like you're driving an arcadey tank that can just plow through any car | i can hit an oncoming car at mph and take no damage but slightly nudge a stationary vehicle and almost die missions: there are four different types of missions that are repeated throughout the entire game | it's either: killinterrogate this person or stealdestroy something | and all of the racket boss missions reuse the same buildings so there are no more collectibles or money stacks to find and pick up after the first visit ai: i can't remember the last game that had ai this stupid | they can't see more than two feet infront of them so every mission leads to me running around stealth killing everyone without ever getting caught | and if you get bored of that and want to shoot some people have fun with enemies that run at you in the open or poke their head out of the same cover until you shoot them | and once you get a silenced weapon the game becomes a joke | you can clear out an entire warehouse without being careful and no one will notice | two enemies were next to each other talking and i killed one and the other guy kept talking while he took his gun out and walked around for a bit | no reaction to his friend being shot in the head right infront of him cops: are cops even in this game | throughout the entire game i only had to deal with them when the story forced it | i have driven through red lights in the oncoming lane going mph right infront of a police station and gotten nothing more than a little police awareness bar | i've also gone on a massacre and killed everyone in an area and nothing came from it | witnesses to a crime will run past a cop to get to a phone booth instead of just telling the officer that's walking by customization: i thought i hadn't gotten far enough into the game yet but no there is absolutely no customization | there isn't a clothing store or garage in site so you're stuck with lincoln's army jacket and car upgrades are purely performance and not cosmetic weather: the skybox rivals that of old n games and the rain is ugly | the most obvious and possibly the ugliest part of the game is that the time of day changes in waves instead of gradually | if you're driving fast enough you can actually race the time change and stay on the line between morning and afternoon | it is very distracting when it's bright out and then suddenly a wave of darkness comes over everything fps: before the patch i was holding a consistent fps | but since changing it to fps i have been bouncing between fps | my rig is fully capable of running a game like this at max settings at over fps | be upfront with your costumers and tell them that you haven't optimized the game to run at fps instead of leading us on like this the interviews: the idea of having present day interviews with characters from the game was very interesting | but they didn't know when to stop | between every mission they felt like they had to have a short interview cutscene which really breaks the immersion of the game | and there were some parts of the game where i was thinking how the hell i was going to pull the mission off | but then you are promptly interrupted by an interview that spoils the entire mission and that everything went to plan | from the very beginning of the game you already know what happens to lincoln and sal because of what father james says in his interviews overall: this game is a huge disapointment | it has its ups and down like any game but its ups don't carry it very far | i miss the days of mafia with all its little details that showed how much the devs cared | cars had fuel you could shop at or rob every open store stores closed for a day if the employees were killed cops punished you for breaking traffic laws cops kept track of your license plate and clothing so that you had to change them and every mission was vital to the story and didn't feel like a filler side mission | the thing about this game is that it does nothing new | the story while enjoyable is very predictable | and every game mechanic that is present or missing has been done times better before | the godfather which is a year old game accomplished more than this game | wait until a huge patch comes out or until the game is at most $ | hangar and k thank you for treating a huge demographic as second class citizens with this abysmal and lazy port

review_text: if you don't feel like reading this entire thing the long and short of it is that as a very steadfast mafia fan this is not only a disservice to the series but to this style of open world game | throughout most of my playtime i was planning on keeping the tagline to this review 'mafia iii isn't a bad game but | ' however after i spent more and more time with the game i can no longer say it isn't a bad game | there are many factors that play into this and it's unfortunate that they are also the factors that comprise roughly ninety percent of the game | first and foremost many of the negative reviews on here mention repetition to an extreme degree | they're correct though i wouldn't say the repetition is what kills it after all gtav is a series of missions to drive a car somewhere and shoot people as well but the fact that there's so little variation to the main gameplay loop | this consists of driving to a location of roughly a dozen enemies getting out of your car and killing them all while also doing a few tiny extra things like destruction or interrogation | this wouldn't be so bad if they were more substantial or involved but sadly they all take roughly a minute to do and then you have to drive around and do another exact copy of this same activity | it's extremely grating | beyond that there's the driving | this is hands down the absolute worst open world driving i've experienced in years | it's really two different parts that combine into a horrible whole | the first is the fact that the cars handle terribly | this is to be expected as it has been with the previous two mafia games and the cars drive like the vehicles of the period would | but they seem to be worse off and harder to control than the older and lesser vehicles from the past two games | when you add on to this the second and far more egregious problem of how the environment handles these cars the experience is incredibly unpleasant | nearly every object in the game including bushes and small objects act like solid concrete blocks that weigh more than your car | a light tap or grazing of anything will instantly stop your car dead in its tracks | several smaller objects and the railroad tracks also have the ability to send your car flying literally thirty feet in the air while flipping end over end | this truly is the worst open world driving i've experienced in many many years | another mark against the game is the ai | the previous two titles never had anything resembling good ai but somehow in this one the npcs have regressed in both combat and driving ability even further | the combat ai has a habit of either shooting from behind cover endlessly or blindly charging past your cover | this leads to frustration in that the game was designed as a cover-based shooter and you weren't meant to have bullet-sponge enemies charging past you and shooting you in the back | the traffic ai is worse than usual open world fare and the cop chases deserve special mention | the cop ai is tenacious and uses a system akin to gtaiv | you have a circle of intrigue where they will chase you and all you need to do is exit this circle to throw them off | sadly the game has a habit of spawning police cruisers directly in front of you during a chase and have them ram you | this refreshes the circle heavily damages your vehicle while bringing it to a dead stop and allows the cars you were outrunning to catch up | they also have sniper-like accuracy while firing from a moving vehicle and routinely destroy your tires which ruins the car's already poor handling | add to this the aforementioned issue with minor obstacles completely stopping your car and the chases are infinitely frustrating | beyond the design flaws are the technical ones | the game has many triggers or scripts that are easily and unintentionally broken | in the past five hours i played tonight i had a mission-centric npc that was following me get locked out of the room we were supposed to enter which broke a separate script and left him unable to open doors for me to exit i punched an npc through a cage containing our fight which left him orbiting the ring outside unable to continue the fight and had a mission-centric vehicle not register that i had gotten into it or that i blew it up in an attempt to reset it | the game will often spawn a copy of something inside of itself leading to cars suddenly and randomly exploding fifty feet into the air and a hilarious series of doppelgangers of your main cohorts in the storyline | this is in addition to the dozens of crashes i've had to endure while attempting to make progress in the game | there is some good in this game | the main story its missions and the writing dialog and voice acting are all first rate and top notch | they're a return to mafia form and these highlights almost make the game worth suffering through to get to | the visuals are fantastic and the lip syncing and facial expressions are deserving of extra praise | the gunplay feels fairly good though is still a step down from the previous two titles | it's probably the main saving grace of the game considering that the repetitive main gameplay loop relies on so much combat wherever you go | there's also a surprisingly functional stealth system included with the game as well | the main problem with mafia iii is that the vast majority of what it gives to you as its core gameplay is the exact same as the boring cleanup activities you'd do in any other open world game when you're working your way to % | instead of being fun main missions or interesting things to do you're stuck running from place to place to place quickly doing something and moving to the next one | despite having a wealth of collectibles already in the game the actual missions the game tasks you with feel like even more collecting making the overall product a horrible slog that i can't find enough redeeming qualities in to make any sort of recommendation |

to marcano meaning lincoln requires the help of underbosses cassandra vito scaletta and thomas burke | as you recruit each of these lieutenants you'll gain a variety of perks like an arms dealer a consigliere to collect your cash a hit squad to help out in a fight or vehicle delivery but retaining these means keeping your underbosses happy | as you gain control of each of new bordeaux's rackets more diplomatic approach divvying turf up equally between all three | failing to keep an underboss happy however will push them out turning them into an enemy that lincoln will have to deal with | it means the decisions you make during sit downs can have real consequences so you'll need to choose wisely | there are some facets of mafia that you'll need to think about then although for the most part the game's missions are largely variations on the same objective sending you into hostile territory to clear out criminal scumbags | little things like wiretapping junction boxes using fuses also reveals enemy positions other racket locations and collectibles in the region on the mini map making life easier for yourself | an accomplished cover shooter at its core practically every one of the rackets you seize comes from clearing out heavily armed goons whether via stealthy means or through a more gung-ho approach | as such you can expect to be stacking up the bodies murdering enforcers interrogating informants who can be recruited if you'd rather not kill them and inflicting damage to the racket by destroying stashes of drugs chemicals or whatever | it can actually get rather repetitive | thankfully mafia 's shooter mechanics are fantastic as are the rest of the game's open-world systems like the fun driving model that includes a more realistic 'simulation' option that can be toggled on or off or the brutal and gratifying melee combat | by the time you reach the latter stages of mafia you'll be a well-oiled killing machine able to pull off brutal kills and headshots with aplomb | unfortunately mafia is hampered by a whole litany of bugs and other issues most of which are odd visual quirks including some lighting weirdness numerous instances of pop-in nutty soundtrack too is utterly stellar stuff delivering the best of s music and bringing its version of a tumultuous new orleans to startling life | the tunes blaring out of the radio from the likes of the rolling stones the beach boys creedence clearwater revival jimi hendrix and others are one of the best bits of mafia | the game's excellent storyline also keeps things ticking along nicely intercut with present day documentary-style sequences and donovan's testimony telling the tale of lincoln clay's vengeful mission from the perspective of the people who were there at the time | it's a great narrative device although there are certain scenes that recount what happened before you've actually had the chance to play out the ensuing scenario | nonetheless mafia 's story is fantastic unflinchingly violent and authentic in its rendition of a turbulent time and place | definitely not for the faint-hearted hangar 's open-world is one that's riddled with rampant racism sex drugs and destroy x killcapture this guy | infact after playing through the entire game i can only remember one mission being somewhat different | there is a stealth option to let you mix things up more on that review_text: fallout is a game that's good but not great | i love the changes to power armor and although i think they shouldn't have put your first set of armor so early in the game the jet pack which unfortunately takes way too long to unlock is an absolute blast to use and really highlights the more vertical nature of the commonwealth over fallout 's map | the enemies are much more fun to fight both because of the shooting being significantly improved and because of the enemies' new animations and attacks like mole rats tunneling under the ground and ghouls dodging out of your aim | i love the new companions and the inclusion of romance and a few companion quests even though the ai pathing is still kind of awful and they still have too much trouble entering elevators | the main campaign is generally a lot more interesting than in and feels more original and the different faction branches make it feel like it's going to be a lot more replayable than most bethesda games are even though it does lose a lot of momentum near the end | even the removal of skills surprised me since despite being obvious oversimplification the perk chart is actually fairly balanced and even after hours of playing i still hadn't maxed out every skill i wanted despite maxing out every skill period in fallout within or so | the graphics are good enough that i don't think i'll be needing any mods for that any time soon and the new vault suits make my butt look just fantastic | it's not without its problems though | fallout is a great shooter and a great adventuring game but it's not much for roleplaying | the dialogue system is extremely limited and even with the mod that makes each choice more than one word you're still typically limited to 'yes yes with more dialogue no ask a question' as your choices and you never get more than | the character being voiced makes it hard to keep your own character in mind because of how overly soft-spoken they tend to be even in the 'mean' choices and skills that added flavor in the past like black widow no longer have any special dialogue or events instead being reduced to generic percentage bonuses | there are no dialogue checks for anything except speech anymore and speech is just one of three difficulty levels based on your charisma skills | save-scumming has been revolutionized with the ability to quick save in the middle of dialogue and even just turn to the side and shove a bunch of chems and beer down your throat to pass skill checks | the dialogue system as a whole feels very simplified and makes the game feel more like borderlands with light rpg elements instead of fallout | the legendary monsters add on to this feeling essentially functioning as the equivalent of badass enemies from borderlands instead of being the rare one-of-a-kind enemies that you found in special areas that were fun to encounter like in the previous games | the ui is awful and aside from the fact that it looks like a unity placeholder it's just generally not very functional and the changes to the pip boy navigation seem to have no purpose other than to annoy you such as making it so that you can't see all five inventory buttons at once anymore instead having to scroll between them not that it matters since my pip boy disappeared due to a glitch and never came back around halfway in but still | the weapon customization comes at the price of there not being very much actual weapon variety and most of the unique weapons are just renamed versions of the generic ones with a stat buff removing the thrill of finding a cool unique weapon in some random building while exploring | the weapon balance is also somewhat off and you can mod pistols to do more damage than the most highly modified | caliber sniper rifle or tommy guns that do more damage than miniguns | repeating quests are still unfortunately a thing and they still don't actually tell you which ones are repeating and you'll likely always have at least two clogging your quest list because of the minutemen whining at you | the settlement building system feels like a half finished mod that somehow accidentally got included in the finished game and even if it had a tutorial the system barely works at times and the buttons are all mapped to the same things for no explainable reason other than 'consoles' so if you want to press e to choose something from the building menu to build you have to make sure you're not looking at literally anything else in the settlement or you'll just end up moving it around instead | overall i think fallout is a massive step up from fallout in almost every way possible and definitely the best time i've had playing an unmodded bethesda game but as far as being a roleplaying game i think new vegas review_text: edit: at hours so far i think i can review the game in its entirety | this will be a long review since i'll be comparing fallout to the two previous bethesda installments | a tl;dr can be found near the bottom | i loved fallout | it explored a world last left alone by interplay a good number of years ago | it came back around via bethesda's production and imagination bringing you an unpretty post-apocalyptic experience | it let players explore the game in their own right making moral questions along their experience | fallout: new vegas took from the atmosphere of fo and expanded upon that | i grew to love nv even more than fo | not only did it capture the fallout universe even more but the gameplay mechanics were far more intuitive and expansive | with that being said i strongly like fallout but quite can't love it in its current state | as a fallout game it's not as good as the previous two games released by bethesda | i like to think of it in the same vein as dark souls versus dark souls : the second game was great in its own right but the overall experience was largely forgettable compared to the first one | ----------- for the cons: fallout feels very watered down and shallow compared to the previous games | they discarded the karma system and skill levels | everything having to do with improving your character's abilities is done solely by perks | while the other games' perks felt exactly like the definition of the word a system complementing one's play-style now it's a forced simplified leveling system | the skill levels of past games influenced passive traits and skill checks helping a player notice their character change and grow in subtle ways within the overall world | i was hoping the leveling system was a bit similar to skyrim: while it wasn't perfect your skills increased based on actions made in real-time and you could only choose certain perks after reaching certain skill levels | carrying the simplified theme there are only main factions in this new installment with several other minor factions that largely don't interact with you other than simply having to kill them | previous installments didn't necessarily have more per se but you could choose how you could interact with them | in fallout you could either side or go against certain factions and actually interact with them | in fallout: nv you could be more diplomatic and choose whether certain minor factions ally or become enemies with certain major factions | in fallout it's simply kill-on-sight save for a couple minor factions which don't add to the bigger picture | as a consequence the world feels ironically less alive | while fallout is larger than the other games' maps the lack of independent settlements doesn't make it feel like you're stepping into a different world | i suppose that was bethesda's way of showing that it's still a post-apocalyptic setting but the other games' populations made you feel like they were struggling to survive | this game simply feels empty | the quests in this game aside from the main quests suffer from the redundant quests commonly found in mmorpgs go kill this enemy or retrieve this item return receive xp and repeat said formula | no depth no interesting side story just errands | the lack of a karma system means you can't feel your character make decisions contributing to their overall moral standpoint | other reviewers touched on the fact you can only choose four options within context-sensitive dialogue | in my opinion it isn't that the four options aren't inherently bad in their own right but that the four options don't really contribute to any long-lasting consequences or effects | aside from ultimately deciding which of the four major factions you side with you eventually have to agree with most characters whether you want to or not | ------- now for some good points which are still somewhat partial: the crafting system is interesting | you can mod weapons armor and clothing which takes some influence from skyrim | depending on your play-style you can customize your character to be more stealth-based full-melee a heavy gunner or a hybrid | it gives you many different ways to play that aren't as initially apparent | the settlement-building system is one point i liked | it's a bit janky initially as certain pieces don't lock into certain places | however it can be mostly optional if you choose to play that way | it feels like you're actually rebuilding the commonwealth | it wasn't fully hashed out in my opinion because settler management can get annoying | the only way to tell who is assigned to what is by seeing it in first-person via line-of-sight as opposed to a menu showing the breakdown of the system in play | however i can appreciate bethesda's ambitions on settlement-building so it's not quite a con to me | with certain perks you can link your settlements together and see your control grow over the commonwealth | what fallout lacks in expansiveness among multiple factions and faction interaction it excels in your ultimate choice on which major faction to side with | there are no inherently good or bad factions your decisions depending on the type of person you are will take some time and consideration | the leveling system goes on indefinitely too | while i hate the redesigned perkleveling system it seems to have been put in place with the thought in mind that one could play indefinitely and continuously improve your character | i like that it's so gradual that you never feel like you're done with your character | a weird consequence in my own experience is that the beginning of the game feels harder than other games then you reach a particular plateau where you end up steamrolling over everything then it becomes hard again when your weapons no longer do as much damage to higher-leveled enemies forcing one to have to adapt their play-style accordingly | i personally like leveling in that aspect | combat in this game is a clear winner over previous games | vats moves slowly as opposing to pausing causing you to make quick decisions on where you hit your targets | weapons feel like actual weapons versus being just weapon models | revamping power armor was a very nice touch | they feel heavy powerful and you can customize them to nearly any play-style as well | the graphics are quite pretty | from my standpoint i think it'll depend on how you feel about it within the context of the game | fallout and new vegas now looks slightly dated compared to fallout but in my opinion they captured the roughness of a post-apocalyptic environment | this game while very pretty doesn't look like the aftermath of a nuclear attack | ----- overalltl;dr: fallout is a good game in its own right if you're new coming into the fallout universe | very accessible to the new player without getting too complex | if you played fallout and new vegas this new game isn't necessarily bad it's still a fun game but the features that became staples in the previous installments were either simplified or left behind | i still recommend this game because ultimately it's a fun game | i loved fallout and new vegas; i | controls are smooth directional pad things with those arrow symbols can be used to control almost every menu now you are not forced to click with a mouse on a symbol that requires luck to hit reliably new vegas gunplay has taken a massive step forward as now you can shoot by yourself and are not forced to use vats which was disgusting in previous fallout tittles | crafting is just awesome review_text: do like rpg games | do you love the fallout franchise | if so you may want to hold off on purchasing fallout | fallout is the next entry in the fallout franchise taking place years after fallout and years after fallout new vegas | while there was a lot of excitement for fallout when it was first announced it has sadly fallen short in almost every capacity | lets start off with the good parts of fallout | graphics: fallout is a beautiful game | it may not have the best graphics out there but even when being played on low settings it is still quite pleasing to the eye | if you add in the fact that you can mod it taking into consideration the games engine you can pull of a level of graphics that would rival the best looking games on the market possibly for quite some time | mods: fallout has a huge amount of mod support with mods being available for console users as well when they get it finished | this enables you to customise your game in virtually any way you see fit without the need to buy a pc in order to do it | music: the music is done very well there are a lot new songs while at the same time some of our favorites from fallout have made a return | sadly though that is about as generous as i can be and it goes down hill from here | for the negatives we will start with the big issues and narrow it down from there | bugs: you would think after doing the fallout franchise for so long they would figure out that they need to get rid of the bugs and glitches before the game is released to the public | there is a reason games go through alpha and beta testing with multiple stages of testing for each and multiple paths until they get things running smoothly | bethesda has not managed to get that down though and much like the launches of previous titles in the series bugs and glitches were rampant in fallout 's launch | while bethesda has patched a few of the glitches and is making effort to smooth out the bugs and improve performance that is all stuff that should have been done before the game is released to the public | skills: one of the big draws at least for me to the rpg genre is the skill systems | picking certain skill sets or classes and running with it | in fallout and new vegas this ment picking between small guns energy weapons melee unarmed and many many other skills | fallout has completely removed the skill system from the game and instead runs with a perk based system similar to that which you would find in fps shooters like call of duty | while some people may enjoy this change and think it was the right decision i for one do not as it no longer feels like an rpg with the system it has currently | impact: fallout has always had a setup in which the players choices had an impact on the game | this could be eliminating a faction and it's members no longer being in the game world | it could also be something as simple as the cut scenes showing a different outcome at the end based on the decisions you made | fallout new vegas took this idea to the next level and made it so just about everything you did impacted the game | from what towns you helped out to what companions you did side quests for or decided to ignore to what factions you decided to help or take out and ending in which of the major factions you sided with in the end if you sided with one at all | all of these decisions were reflected in the end cutscenes discribing to you what kind of impact your decisions had on the game world as a whole | fallout on the other hand is seriously lacking in this department | after having gone through the main story line and played for about hours i don't feel as though i made any impact at all on the game world | yes you choose which factions you help out and which you destroy like in previous games but there is no impact overall | if you choose to eliminate faction a their members with the exception of leadership still exist in the game and there are no cutscenes at the end describing what impact you had | the cutscene they do have is very generic and bland having one scene to fit of the major factions and a second scene to fit for the th faction which doesn't really differ all that much | vats: vats was a huge part of fallout and new vegas | it had its issues yes but it was very important non the less | if you ran into trouble and group of enemys is waiting for you around the corner you just took you enabled vats and took the time to plan out your attacks | in fallout vats is still there although in a different capacity | time no longer comes to a stand still when you activate vats and instead just slows down | while this makes the game sound more challenging at first in practice it just ends up causing more problems then anything else | with the camera freaking out on you trying to keep up and increases number of line of sight issues being among the top of the list | vats really doesn't seem worth it in the long run in fallout | rollplay: the first word in rpg stands for rollplay | it is very difficult to get into a rollplay with your character when you have a voiced protaganist | decide you want to be evil in your playthrough | how evil do you think you can be when your character sounds like a happy peaceful person from | this along with some of the previous mentioned issues kills the rollplay and the replay factors that drive most people to the fallout franchise | ron perlman: i know i know i am kind of nitpicking here but lets face it | ron perlman is the voice of fallout | he is the narrator for every fallout game released so far starting back at fallout | he also has other roles in the fallout universe like playing butch harris in the original fallout | in fallout though he gets a very short part as a tv anchorman at the begining of the game that lasts less then a minute | bethesda you can't do this to us ron perlman is fallout | the final thing i am going to touch on is the shady business practices of bethesda during fallout | when they announced the game orignally they bragged about it's difficulty system and how it ended in survival difficulty | a mode which boasts % damage for the player % damage for the enemys slower hp regen via food and stimpacks and an increased spawn rate for legendary enemys | they also bragged about how if that was not hard enough for you the huge amount of mod support the game would have when the creation kit was released would let you increase the difficulty as much as you would like | this would be similar to skyrim players that used mods like frostfall hunger overhaul hypothermia cloaks of skyrim and many other mods to make skyrim more challenging to them | after months of the game being released though some people starting complaining that the game was not difficult enough and the creation kit was not available yet for them to mod their game to make it more challenging | bethesda's response to this was to do a new game mode called survival which would revamp damage include hunger thirst sleep and other things and overall make the game more difficult | this was fine at first the problem though was in doing so bethesda eliminated the original survival difficulty completely and has told players that liked it to either mod their game to get it back or play on a lower difficulty setting | this is very very bad business practices on behalf of bethesda and a very disappointing move from what was one of my favorite developers | in the end fallout is a very lackluster game that does not feel like a fallout game and instead is more like a post apocalyptic call of duty | i would highly advise you skip this game and spend your money on something else | if you are into rpg games get something like dark souls or one of the many other rpgs out there | if you are into other genres there are a ton of better options for you | tldr: fallout is a very unimpressive game |

review_text: war never changes runs the tagline for fallout and though that's a dour descriptor for this sometimes bleakly hilarious game it's also sort of true that the fallout series hasn't really changed | however that's because of another important saying: if it ain't broke don't fix it | short of changing the setting to the boston area circa bethesda game studios simply hasn't had to tinker with much since 's near-perfect fallout: new vegas | the big new questionable improvement is basically the inclusion of a built-in mod kit which allows players to fix up their liberated settlements | as it turns out it's a bit more onerous to construct things on a d plane as opposed to the d plane of the game's mobile prequel fallout shelter | it's also largely unnecessary to waste skill points on perks like gun nut that allow for deeper customization on one's arsenal given that every slain foe drops everything they're wearing | then again this only enhances the realism of the game both in terms of the cobbled-together post-apocalyptic aesthetic and in the freedom given to those who want to play through on their own terms | but fallout is far more than an expansion | without spoiling too much the plot introduces a new creature beyond the standard irradiated monsters like the bearish yao guai and self-descriptive bloatflies and feral ghouls | these new foes or potentially friends are synths robots that are all but indistinguishable from humans | it's blade runner in all the right ways and most of the moral story-altering dilemmas presented this go-around revolve around which of the various factions players choose to support from those in the railroad who want to set the enslaved synths free to the familiar faces of the brotherhood of steel who want to destroy that dangerous technology | the core of fallout 's journey centers on your character and his or her quest to find the truth about what happened in vault | though the last two fallout games put you smack in the center of an involved narrative it never felt as personal or invested as fallout 's story | that's largely due to fallout 's committal to giving the player character voiced dialogue | the typical silent protagonist is gone and bethesda's taken a bit of a bioware approach to giving the player a meaningful connection to the in-game avatar | your story will play out with dialogue choices you selected and just by having an actor there to give some inflection to the words bethesda is able to make you more connected to this persona than ever before | while conversational choice has been a part of the fallout series talking it out with computer characters face-to-face was always a bit disjointed | it never felt natural | with fallout there's a more cinematic approach to conversations | the camera always pulls out to find a more appealing angle to show the different sides of a conversation | there's a large emphasis on making your character more a part of this world by showing him or her from outside the default first-person perspective and it makes a great deal of difference in connecting you to this person this world and the conversations you'll have | conversations are equally as important to fleshing out your relationship with the numerous companions you'll meet on your adventure | unlike previous entries in the series these characters actually feel like companions | whether it's dogmeat piper codsworth or any of the others you'll encounter and befriend there's more to having these people around than just serving as another gun in battle or a walking storage unit | the longer you hang out with a single companion the more your relationship with that person will grow | characters will talk with you while on quests and your decisions no matter how minor will impact how they perceive you | complements to the so-called main campaign aside the majority of a player's time in fallout is spent wandering around the commonwealth especially now that bethesda has removed the level cap and it's the setting that ultimately needs to hold up as a central character | those who were skeptical that bostona less immediately familiar setting than washington d | c | or review_text: fallout is a really difficult game to talk about | although the box up there is marked 'no' i don't think this is an explicitly bad game | in fact there are a lot of really good things here | to be honest bethesda has built a fantastic world even if it is a bit small | the commonwealth is packed full of well-designed places to explore and the interior zones that you can go into generally have some kind of unique story that has happened within them | terminals and notes will tell you a direct story but there are indirect things to observe too like a corpse huddled in a collapsed crawlspace with some candles and a survival kit | the unique dungeons that you'll come across have lots of tiny little stories like this that make for a very immersive experience | even though the total area size is relatively small especially when compared to other open world games of the past few years it is densely packed with places to explore | bethesda has also gone ahead and made the gunplay satisfying frantic and well-paced | whereas fallout and new vegas had very awkward combat at times the enemies in fallout behave in a much better fashion | ghouls will crawl out from under cars and through windows | bugs will ambush and surround you | raiders and other enemies with guns will actually take cover and seemingly work somewhat as a team rather than throwing themselves at you in a single-file line | they'll even throw grenades taunt you and lose track of you | vats is still pretty overpowered though but it is entirely optional to use if you want to avoid being too powerful | the once hated level-scaling bethesda is infamous for actually ends up working out really well here | areas that are too dangerous for you are generally packed full of legendary enemies that are still way ahead of your level but in general you'll never have quests that are way too easy because you've outlevelled them and this allows you to tackle the content entirely at your leisure | you can explore freely and do things as you please rather than feeling pressured to do something because you'll be trivializing it due to levelling too high | if i stopped here fallout sounds like a great game | hell it kind of is a great experience and i easily see myself getting at least twenty or thirty more hours out of it | i'll probably play the dlc at some point too | i've had a pretty good time exploring the commonwealth taking quests here and there and enjoying the implicit stories scattered across the nuclear wasteland | i will say that if you're the type of gamer who just wants a good solid experience you really can't go too wrong with fallout | if you've played bethesda games before you know what to expect | and herein lies the problem | bethesda has walked the line between making casual experiences and deep experiences for awhile | connotations of these terms aside a pretty common complaint since oblivion has been that bethesda questlines are simple; dialogue is often boring quests aren't too varied with their goals and ultimately the game feels kind of empty | however all of their games seem to have just enough depth to them to keep you engaged for a long time | you can almost always find something new when you boot up a bethesda game for a new run through it | but fallout is different | there aren't really any branching questlines impactful decisions or choices to make | there is a distinct lack of variance in the quest goals and nearly everything boils down to 'go somewhere kill a bunch of enemies maybe pick up an item of some kind come back | ' you cannot talk your way out of combat there is no alternate stealth route and the path is clearly laid out for you | dialogue choices boil down to 'yes sarcastic yes more information please no but i'll do it later | ' there are exactly four choices and three of them do the same thing | you can try to alter the path of a quest by being snarky but it will change nothing | there are tons of wasted opportunities across the wasteland and you'll come across many interesting setpieces that ultimately are combat zones | twisted art gallery | combat zone | black market arena | yet another combat zone | technologically the game is a mess | the same bugs that were present ten years ago in oblivion are still here | npcs will continue to block doors end up in strange places or act in strange ways | i had one escort quest where i entered a new area with the guy i was guarding and in the new area he appeared hundreds of steps out-of-bounds | i had to solve the quest with noclip | i've had my companion walk into a wall while talking to me | i've ended up with two npcs talking to each other but facing different directions | i've had questgivers standing on inaccessible roofs for no good reason | the engine is tied to your fps so things can sometimes speed up and down depending on how smooth your game is | speaking of performance my system has been able to max out every single game i've thrown at it built in december with top-of-the-line parts and yet fallout seems to stutter for no reason in strange places | fire and certain angles while in dense areas will kill my framerate for no discernable reason while intense heated gun-battles in busy areas will stay a solid fps | i had to spend an hour tinkering with | ini files to get rid of silly problems like mouselag in menus mouse xy being different speeds a claustrophobic fov for p and even then not all of my problems are actually fixed | i can hardly believe that this was deemed okay in and we're three major patches in | fallout is a terrible rpg and a bad fallout game but it is a good game | i am unhappy with the fact that this is fallout but i can't say that i haven't had a good time | while the glaring problems are certainly taking away from my enjoyment of the game it's a pretty fun light rpg with major fps elements | if you go in with no expectations and don't expect an iterative improvements over bethesda's previous games you'll have a good time | there isn't a great story here quests are repetitive the dialogue is bad there are no choices the engine is ancient and needs to be put out to review_text: i could write a thesis on the topic of fallout s game design at this point but ill try to keep it brief: fallout is a good game | its not a great game and its an extremely flawed game but i think its a good game nonetheless | fallout is the third entry in the modern fallout saga taking place in the post-apocalyptic boston massachusetts area commonly referred to by its denizens as the commonwealth | the player takes the role of the sole survivor: the only dweller of vault to make it through all out nuclear war after being cryogenically frozen | the only survivor that is except for your son who is mysteriously removed from the vault while you helplessly remain locked within your cryogenic pod | with the world destroyed and with no other reason to live the sole survivor sets off on a quest to find their son | from there fallout follows the cookie-cutter bethesda rpg formula | wander to a quest point talk to someone to learn where to go next go to next quest point kill loot return gain status in a particular faction rinse repeat | there are quite a few things that fallout does well and theres quite a few things that bethesda added or changed to freshen up the experience | the map of boston for example is the biggest and most lush fallout world yet with tons of nooks and crannies to explore | weapon and armor crafting have been significantly revamped to provide lots more variety and options for customization and crafting | the perk and attribute systems have been completely overhauled to allow players the freedom to make the superpowered protagonist of their dreams | combat has been improved and its much more enjoyable getting into firefights and melee battles with enemies than it was in previous titles | theres also a new settlement management feature that allows players to build and manage their own settlements across the wasteland | even with all these new features however fallout still feels fairly unremarkable | the biggest problem is fallout takes away the players agency | youre no longer a lone wolf type trying to survive in a dog-eat-dog world making tough decisions to ensure your own well-being that impact yourself and the world around you | nope now you are the protagonist and as such you can only do things that bethesda imagined the protagonist would do | theres literally only a handful of choices in fallout that have any meaningful impact | when speaking to an npc who is trying to deliver a quest generally your only option is to ask more about it accept the quest or accept the quest with a condescending tone | you cant tell them bug off | you cant tell them to bug off and then warn the opposing faction of their plan and lead their enemies to their doorstep | you can skill check every once in awhile but its hardly ever an option and hardly are the results significant when you can | unfortunately this is what kills fallout for me: the story and choices you can make in this game are all terrible | theres literally no karma system anymore | the game forces you to side with one of four equally terrible factions all with poorly explained completely rigid motives in order to complete the main story-line | and take it from me the payoff isnt worth it no matter who you choose | if what you love about fallout and bethesda games is simply exploring finding cool gear leveling up ad nauseam and then crushing every ghoul and raider in your path then you will probably enjoy this game | that portion of fallout is still alive and well in fallout and is why i still found something to like about it because i really enjoy all of those things too | if youre looking for a deep rpg experience with memorable characters tough choices and an engaging plot fallout is severely lacking | this one gets my cautious recommendation |

review_text: i have a bit of a mixed opinion on this game | while it was entertaining enough for me to finish looking back i can't say it was worth $ plus $ for the season pass which i got a discount for | there are some positives though | the graphics are good by bethesda's standards nothing outstanding but pretty good and the soundtrack is beautiful | the one thing that bethesda did an amazing job on however was the follower system | easily the best of any bethesda game that i've played to date | followers have a whole lot of dialogue both situational and dialogue with the player | you have an actual dynamic relationship with your follower and you can even have a romantic one if you want | different followers prefer that you do different things for example lockpicking theft or instead doing nice things etc | and some will even leave your service if you displease them too much | for example a more kindly follower will leave if you murder a whole bunch of innocent people | followers will even have unique conversations with citizens of diamond city which i found quite intriguing | simply walking around and experiencing the map is surprisingly fun | as with previous titles from bethesda the map is littered with unmarked locations which can add to the atmosphere a good deal | sometimes it's pleasant to not focus on quests and just wander around aimlessly | following the occasional radio signal to its source for example is interesting enough especially because bethesda was smart enough not to slap a marker on most of them | listening to tapes and reading through terminals is actually not as boring as it sounds; they include a lot of information about the world and the surrounding areas | searching for special items like the magazines and bobbleheads can be cool too | all of these parts of the game are pretty well-done but unfortunately i can't say the same for the rest | while there are certainly some more exciting scenes the majority of the main questline is fairly uninteresting | i did enjoy the light philisophical dilemma about synths and i especially liked that your relationship with one faction would be harmed if you helped an enemy of theirs too much | however each faction's storyline with the exception of the minutemen was far too similar for my liking | i won't get into the details but there was very little thought put into differentiating them from one another which would have led to a whole lot more playtime | having a voiced protagonist can work well but because fallout does not have a single specific player character other than the default one who matches this voice assigning a voiced protagonist takes away from immersion in virtually all playthroughs | i also did not enjoy the backstory that bethesda sloppily placed on my character again takes a lot away from the rpg elements of the game | the sheer number of interactions that required me to talk about my son in one way or another in order to progress was a little off-putting | i just want to be able to ignore things like that until i'm ready | furthermore the dialogue system is absolutely terrible it looks like a dumbed-down version of daggerfall's for goodness' sake | you have no more than four options for all npc interactions | i normally don't mind this amount at all but i realized very quickly that the different options are frequently a slightly different way of getting the exact same result | your categories are usually something along the lines of: agree genuine agree sarcastic neutral disagree i'm not exaggerating here | while there are of course actual dialogue lines their meaning is ridiculously simple and limiting | i wasn't a fan of the inventory but for the most part i was able to look past that after all it's a pip-boy | the thing that really bothered me was the local map | besides being a jumbled mess [www | gameranx | com] the game only lets you look at a tiny area around your current location enough to fill the screen of your pip-boy but very little more even if you have already been to that area | combined with awful interior level design this makes navigating through buildings a nightmare for completionists and casuals alike | level design is of the utmost importance in any game; you don't think twice about good level design until you've come across something really bad | whoever designed the majority of fallout 's interiors has no idea how to build anything that doesn't frustrate the player for a game with great level design see doom | insignificant-looking doorways are commonly the actual way forward in a dungeon whereas gradiose important-looking doorways commonly lead to side passages or to the exact same place as a much smaller door | what's the point of making a door that attracts your attention if it's just going to be squandered | additionally far too many interiors are hopelessly jumbled and have a very unintuitive layout further contributing to the confusion | i will give them some credit though; some important doors are painted red making them stand out in a still-believable fashion | however this is totally inconsistent as many uniquely marked doors don't lead anywhere special at all | i also can't help but point out that most interiors look very similar | the layout is obviously somewhat different in each building but very few of them stand out even a little bit | i understand needing to stick to certain visual themes and there's nothing wrong with that but when you're almost always unable to tell a dungeon apart from the last there's something wrong with the game | raiding these is actually a lot of fun at first but it gets boring very very quickly once you realize that the vast majority do not offer anything original | another big problem i have with the game is that it's just so buggy | if i didn't have console commands i probably would've given up on the game after a couple days | there are tons of areas in the map that you can get stuck in far too easily wouldn't expect a foot hole to trap you forever after all and have to noclip out of to escape | on many occasions i've witnessed cars animals and enemies flying around like mammoths in skyrim | npcs who are vital to completing quests have mysteriously stopped talking to me in the middle of a quest | my rig i gtx gb ram is just barely under the recommended system requirements | while the game runs fine on high settings ~-fps depending on the area i actually get a very similar performance in the witcher on ultra which is a significantly more graphically demanding game | i think this shows that fallout is not optimized as well as it could be | todd howard claimed that fallout had a solid hours of content | i've done every quest found every location and i have % of the achievements | i've literally completed everything the game has to offer including all of the dlc content and i was only able to get a little over hours out of the game for
