review_text: something about the beth-rpg is so pure innocent and addictingly fun they're impossible to put down impossible to not appreciate | the problem is fallout is deeply flawed regardless of my boundless love and addiction for it | as a rabid fan of obsidian's superb new vegas i've realised the 'formula' for the beth-rpg is bulletproof | what cannot be replicated is the nuance of the true avatars and world of an rpg | fallout unfortunately lacks many of the rpg mechanics of it's predecessors and is far more in line with a borderlands title | it's a 'looter-shooter' where you upgrade customize your guns find new ones and explore a gorgeous world | all negativity aside | it's a fun addicting fps with an expansive open world | aesthetic she ain't a looker as far as texture resolution and overall graphical power goes | blurry close-up textures aside the overall presentation is actually fantastic | the world is colorful and intricately designed from curving futuristic skyscrapers to decrepit wooden shacks with streams of fabric tied around the beams to verdant trash laden radioactive plains and clawing nuclear winter trees | character models are actually capable of expressing emotion | lighting is superb with glorious sunsets casting god rays through trees or the glaring illumination and stark shadows of fenways spotlights | there is also an impressive shamble and clutter to crumbling city streets or shot laden bars | gun models are satisfactory with appropriately complex laser weaponry gleaming blades gunpower stained firearms and plenty of random knobs and buckles alongside glowing sights | youll see tons of 'holy-' vistas and even some crowded bullet riddled rooms you can slowly pan around as a candle burns in the corner and desk fans shadow whirls on a nuka cola poster studded wall | sound guns sound fine | nice crack crisp explosion blunt strike perfectly satisfactory | the wasteland eerily quiet with bursts of distant gunfire and screams of terrifying wildlife haunting the silence | stalking through buildings is accompanied by crackling fires and hummin electricity urban areas have appropriate bustle | a huge letdown however is the radio | little new songs were added | i actually turned the radio off and am so glad i did because the ambient score is criminally underappreciated | the soft piano of wasteland travel is both unsettling and hopeful while combat is heavily drummed and quickens the pulse immediately | faction themes are especially notable from the heroic horn of the brotherhood to furtive and optimistic electronica of the railroad | im listening to it as i write in fact | combat fps gameplay is revamped and drastically improved from previous games | aside from more nimble aiming and hady kickback from big guns general motion is far smoother and more human than nv and | peaking from cover to empty a rifle mag from the hip at an enemy has never felt better more so when you sprint forward to smack him across the head with the stock and once more onto his kneeling back | the ai of npcs has improved with enemies and companions scrounging for more effective weapons utilizing turrets and grenades flanking sticking to cover suppressing and creating actual search patterns with chilling dialogue too | as a rule of thumb enemies with visible armour pieces bosses and legendaries who drop cool status effect loot are subject to traditional rpg hp dragouts cannon fodder infantry increase the chaos and body-count of battle | unfortunately stealth melee and beasts though the modified deathclaws and ghouls are terrifyingly grotesque and swift largely remain the same | vats makes a triumphant return with improved blood and injuries and a slow motion cam | synthetic enemies and ghouls having limbs blown off and still clawing their way across the ground stumps bleedingsparking gave me a sadistic pleasure | guns are diverse with a variety of models and different handling characteristics | roaring shotguns cracking accurate rifles the maelstrom of lead spewing minigun fiery beam lasers blunt and brutal sledgehammers and the horse-kick and flinging impact of a heavy assault rifle | you can also equip your avatar with a variety of creative clothing and armour both for aesthetic and damage protection | power-armour also know functions as a mech with satisfyingly heavy steps hulking mass and resistance to bullets | crafting is also expansive with firearms and armour hosting a score of attachments from extended mags and holo sights to bayonets extra pockets or electric charge | unfortunately thats it | combat consists of armouring up shooting your way through a swarm of enemies trading hp hits with the inevitable boss then bringing home your loot to customize your guns | there are few detective missions diplomatic meetings or hostage rescues quests simply lack the variety and options of approach of prior games | there is no option to sneak through and pickpocket the card key hot wire the vents to close or even convince the enemy to give up | shoot loot and upgrade | setting as usual bethesda knocked it out of the park | specifically fenway park converted into the crowded and ramshackle diamond city populated by catchers mask and pad wearing guards and a center square surrounded by shops with names like home plate | the commonwealth is a terrifically realised world brimming with creative passion from the fleshed-out characters within to the intricately crafted locales | companions are especially impressive and return to the new vegas character progression of old | inquisitive and feisty reporters wise cracking cyborg-detectives or naive killer-robot french | medics | the map is massive and varied from the quaint woods and towns of northern concord down to the commercial high rise-sprawl of downtown boston heading either too the crowded suburbs and docks near the south end or swampy horror of witch trial salem | those of the more adventurous sort can hazmat suit up and head to the glowing sea a radioactive-electric stormed-smoldering-deathclaw ridden hell | scrounge for parts to build up your own settlement with a simply and somewhat intuitive settlement building system | choose from pre-built houses assemble your own from walls and roofs fill it with comfy chairs spotlights machinegun turrets guard towers and walls | build a recruiting beacon and watch as potential merchants farmers and security drift in | you can build some surprisingly comfortable and sprawling outposts with the tools provided | but ultimately my experience in fallout was flawed | in pursuit of an amazing open world and tuned combat the gave up the rpg mechanics which had initially made me love the series | gone are numerous dialogue options replaced by an overly-simplified but voice-acted and well mere options | yes no more info and sarcastic | no longer can my character be charming cunning evil devious hopeful authoritative charismatic romantic ect | this is further worsened by the new skill system | instead of assigning points to categories which unlocked new dialogue or abilities through mastery you are limited to a perk chart | assign points to sets of perks which are arbitrarily assigned to primary attributes you must master to unlock said perks | want to be a stealthy sniper | good luck | your rifle accuracy is determined through a perception perk your headshot chance through a luck perk your damage and stealthiness through some agility perks and your ability to craft a weapon through intelligence perks | honestly i loved my time with this game | i ache for the return of fully realised rpg systems and the death of the dialogue tree | but more so i appreciate the graphical overhaul incredible world and fine-tuned combat | even if it didnt suit my exact and somewhat archaic tastes bethesda made a helluva game | cant wait to start my modded playthrough |

of using console commands but god help you if you're a platform gamer | but really my biggest gripe with this latest installment of fallout is how insubstantial the quests really are ultimately | the few factions that actually matter in this game minutemen railroad brotherhood of steel and institute basically trick and trap you unapologetically into getting into situations that no sane person would ever get into | you are locked into a linear non-variable path with those factions until you reach a critical nexus where a quest for one of those faction requires you to betray or all three of writing is good much better and more natural than fallout ever had | but the system has some problems | sometimes its hard to predict what your character will say when you select a line actually there not a lie | | radiant quests | those semi-random repetitive and usually infinite tasks | im ok with their existence but they should have only unlocked when there is nothing else left to do | or at least moved to a separate quest category | but instead developers decided to mix real hand-crafted quests and random stuff together | if you arent aware of this you can be easily overwhelmed with those infinite tasks and come to a conclusion that most quests in this game suck which is not the case | in fact most hand-made quests are very good | | most towns are locked away or hidden in the beginning | usually fallout games have a lot of towns and player always had a good starting point | in fallout you immediatelly had access to megaton a decent-sized town with interesting characters and quests | fallout 's 'megaton' is your old pre-war hometown and its completely empty in the beginning little more than a playground and settlement-building tutorial | and now to what i like: | the world | its big its great and its very immersive | there are a lot of places you can go to and all of them are hand-made | there you wont find a ton of similar caves tes games are notorious for | in fallout each location is unique and has some kind of backstory | the environments themself are very immersive some places you wont forget for a long time | and ofc its fallout so the world is a little well sometimes not so little crazy in a good way | | rpg | i really like how bethesda approached this aspect of the game even if a lot of people would disagree | fallout was full of pure evil choices and while i think that having a lot of choices is good most of those choices had no sense at all | maybe if you roleplay totally mad psycho they would | but often there was no actual motivation behind those actions | this is also true for some choices in older fallout games in fact they often had harsh penalties for doing something the 'wrong' way and possible rewards were rarely tempting enough | in fallout most choices are morally grey rarely there is a clear good or evil side it resembles a psychological test | what you pick usually depends on your beliefs and information you managed to gather in your adventures | idiologies and beliefs play a major role in this game | and unlike games before it fallout never tries to preach moral characters and factions themself sometimes do but they usually contradict each other and very rarely gives clear answers or solid evidence supporting a single view | it simply makes you do a choice based on your own understanding | this is also why i think there is no usual consequences slide show at the end of the main quest | you make your choices because you believe it will lead to something having developers telling what it 'actually' leads to would destroy this | companions play much bigger role now all of them have their likes and dislikes and occasionally participate in your conversations with other characters | they also often react to the world giving comments about locations or interacting with other characters on their own | | combat and crafting | aside from doing quests and interacting with different characters the main flow of the game is 'explore > kill > loot > craft > explore harder areas' | all steps are important and in my opinion all of them are very well made | the exploration part was covered before this world is worth exploring on its own | then the combat | basically its a shooter st or rd person depending on your preference kinda old school shooter with no cover system or health regeneration which is a good thing in my opinion | the gunplay is solid and doesnt feel clunky like it did in fallout | ofc there are a lot of different weapon types and a nice stealth mechanic to provide more options | vats semi-turnbased auto targeting system is way more usefull thanks to a lot higher actions point regeneration rate | once you kill stuff you grab the loot and improve your equipment with it | the crafting system gives a lot of options its not just for damagedefense improvements you can install a lot of different mods changing items to complement your combat playstyle | another good thing settlements building and development is completely optional you can totally ignore this part and find all stuff you need in the game world | | difficulty and progression | at last bethesda's game thats not a total walk in the park | even on normal first few hours can be challenging harder difficulties especially revamped survival make it brutal | yes you get power armor early in this game so you can feel godlike for a few minutes | but in fact its an old rusty model in very poor condition and only one half-charged power core so dont expect it to be usable for long | also most enemies in this game dont automatically level up with you enemy levels are tied to their zones making leveling up and improving your gear very important and rewarding | overall i highly recommend this game regardless if you played or not previous games |

breached the museum that him and his fellow survivors are taking refuge in | you receive a new quest | typically in a fallout game you will have multiple ways to approach a scenario like this | in review_text: fallout is the fifth major instalment to the fallout series being released on november th for pc ps and xbox one | the game was developed and published by bethesda | if you didnt know already fallout is set in a post-apocalyptic world this instalment is set in boston in the year hundreds of years after a nuclear war | game play in fallout is similar to that of fallout new vegas | you can either play the game in first person mode or third person | personally i found the first person view to be the best but people will want to experiment for their own liking | this game brings a few new game play elements such as a crafting system customizable weapons and base building | i really enjoyed the customizable weapons as it was always something i craved for in new vegas | however i wasnt a massive fan of the base building; for me this aspect was a little dull and uninteresting; building the base seemed pointless as it very rarely did anything of any real use apart from making more resources | you make the base using a crafting system which incorporates every piece of material loot you can find so everything will have some sort of use | you base will attract settlers in which you can assign them tasks such as farming or taking control of artillery for example | along with the new game play features all of the classic elements make a return | the use of pip-boy will aid you in the combat situations letting you select a specific part on your target to shoot | how accurate you are in this mode will depend on your base stats though | fallout is another really expansive open world that allows you to explore to hearts content everywhere is accessible apart from locked doors etc | from when you start the game meaning you can do anything you want right from the word go | the game has four factions in which you can work for and raise your reputation with; but of course working for one will mean consequences with the other so you have to pick wisely | normally i am not a fan of a decision you make in a game means you miss out on content but with this one i didnt mind so much given that the way the story changes and the quest lines adapt to whatever you chose | the graphics in fallout whilst they are good they did seem to fall a little bit short of what i was expecting | mods in the previous two instalments in the franchise are still better looking than this game | that doesnt mean the graphics are bad no no | they are definitely on the upper scale of the market out there right now i was maybe a little overhyped with what to expect but due to being based on the pc mods will surely be released which will make this game absolutely gorgeous and will no doubt make it photo realistic | the game is also fully voice acted to a very high quality the only issue i had with the voice acting side of things was that when you are selecting what to say in a dialog option what you choose can sometimes come out in a different way and i would of actually liked to have seen the actual words you will speak show on screen rather than a summary of the words | i was completely immersed in the story of fallout i was hooked right from the first key point in the game and you are essentially on a search to find your son who was kidnapped | the main story is only one of the plot lines you can follow in the game not only do you have the four factions that you can do missions for you also have plenty of other smaller side quests which also add their own flavour and interesting side plot to the world you are in | the game has some brilliant individual storylines and a lot of them i will remember for a long time | the difficulty in fallout can depend on a couple of things first of all the game has a good number of difficulty settings that you can change on the fly meaning if you find a certain part of the game hard you can drop the difficulty level down to a more manageable level however i was playing on the medium setting and i found the challenge to be just right for me | on top of the regular settings how you play your character will also vary the difficulty of the game if you opt for a more peaceful run you may want to be more stealthy and avoid as much combat as you can where as you can also choose to be all guns blazing and cause as much havoc as possible | i finished the main story and the majority of side quests in the game; i completed it in just over twenty hours | after finishing the main story you are still free to continue you work in the commonwealth allowing you to mop up missions continue crafting and levelling up | there is a season pass available for the game meaning there is going to be dlc in the coming months and not to mention the modability of the game will also mean an almost endless supply of content for you to play | this is going to be another game that you will easily be able to get at least hours out of | the game also has a very high replay ability factor | whether it is playing your character in a different way giving yourself different stats for a different play style or maybe even choosing a different faction to favour towards the end of the game the possibilities of different endings to the game will be more than enough of a reason to play it through at least one more time | technically i didnt have any issues playing fallout | which is a nice surprise given the issues that new vegas had on launch | the game comes with fully customizable controls and the option to play on a controller if you choose | there is also a substantial amount of graphical options meaning you can optimize it for your rig | to round up fallout is going to be considered as a must play title and is definitely going to be one of the top games of the year | the game does almost everything right and keeps the gameplay true to its core | the freedom and creativity you can have in the game just make it an almost perfect game that i cannot find very much wrong with | not to mention the mod support will make this one of the biggest games on the pc platform for the next few years | the games full price of could be considered high for pc but i would honestly say it is worth every penny of that | but we all know how low fallout games can go in sales so if you can wait a few months you may be able to get this for less than if you are lucky but please dont let it stop you review_text: as a huge fan of fallout: new vegas and everything that it did i went into fallout with high expectations that it could live up to the fantastic quality of new vegas | how wrong i was | fallout suffers from the same issue that elder scrolls v: skyrim did; it sacrificed a heavy bulk of the rpg elements from the past games and trades those for a more action-oriented approach | while it does make the game a fair bit more accessible for fans of action games who might be less interested in a more rpg-intensive experience this is a huge negative compared to the rest of the series | as a positive the combat is faster more responsive has a much cleaner style of gunplay and is debatably more engaging than new vegas's due to the higher focus on action elements | however while the combat is solid it is one of two main gameplay elements that is there to hold your interests | and considering how much of the draw from past fallout games comes from the exploration of their post-apocalyptic worlds and interacting with the people and places within it hinging half of what will keep the player invested in the game solely on combat in a world that's mean for an rpg setting is practically shooting yourself in the foot | unfortunately the setting of the commonwealth also doesn't compare to that of the mojave wasteland | as the second major gameplay element comes in the form of a huge crafting system | while skyrim brought in a fairly large crafting system as well as expanding on it with the hearthfire dlc i can still give it a pass since the world of skyrim still had a lot of room for exploration | the commonwealth much to my chagrin almost feels like minecraft at times | instead of admiring the scenery of this post-apocalyptic setting and seeing how civilization changed as a result you're too busy trying to build your own world inside of it | just looking for as many pieces of nuclear materials adhesives or anything else you could possibly need to finish your next big settlement project or modified weapon | this is the biggest warning i can give to anyone who are coming off of fallout or new vegas and are wanting more: you won't find any of theres also an unshakable feeling that its all been staged for you | skyrim would have you believe its a dynamic world thats constantly in flux when in reality its more like a car stuck in neutral waiting to be put into gear | characters go about their daily routines but they merely exist to bestow quests or impart dense records of lore; review_text: the elder scrolls v: skyrim is even with its phenomenal success and enduring popularity a very divisive game amongst the player community and thus fairly difficult to properly review | heralded as an instant classic upon release and absolutely smashing sales it has now fallen into the age-old struggle with oblivion and morrowind in determining which is 'the best' of the series while the true great that is shadowkey stands forgotten not unlike one watching family argue | only joking redguard was clearly better | as much as i would like to spend this entire review wholeheartedly raving about how consistently incredible the modding community is about how time and time again it has brought me back for more; i must unfortunately sidestep it here | instead this review will try to remain objective as possible examining the vanilla game till eventually i hit the character limit and have to cut entire sections as usual | i will personally conclude at the end of the review | beginning with a general note overall if one had to describe the direction that bethesda's game design has taken in recent instalments it would have to be the overall emphasis on creating the world | sure you could argue that that's been the case since the company's inception but the limited technology and balance that they managed to strike with their first few games was a different scenario whereas recently the expansive landscapes and world has come at the cost of so much of what made the elder scrolls great | bound in a far-from arousing opening and destined for the headsman's block you are introduced to the rugged world of skyrim | a civil war between the imperial legion and the nationalistic stormcloaks has been tearing apart the land and tamriel's people for some time and various factions and guilds predominantly the elven supremacists of the thalmor watch warily in the shadows and on the sideline waiting for their chance to strike | political intrigue and constant in-fighting has further increased the almost palpable tensions throughout the country as religion and all forms of reverence comes under increasing scrutiny and persecution | naturally it's not all fun and games from here-on out and the return of the dragons from ancient legends the black wings unfurled amidst blazing sky threatens to once again bring about the end of the world | while the radiant a | i | is busy off eating bread and staring solemnly into space skyrim needs a hero | say you look like you can do it; interested | there's a lot of lore-appropriate speculation that could be used to explain why the region is just so ed-up but regardless it's certainly an intriguing premise to build your character on | if you've played the previous games what you'll immediately notice and most likely be irked by is the omission of traditional classes and meaningful choice in character creation | a 'blank slate' method of levelling up through skill progression rather than the traditional xp system of other rpgs has instead been implemented to encourage the freedom of player choice in the world | the infamous level-scaling mechanic returns and combat has also been 'streamlined' as a result as well as featuring the welcome additions of dual-wielding thanks to the easy-to-use hand allocation system of spells powers and weapons | speaking of which there are plenty with generally great loot on offer and a decent range of ways to obtain it | the evident design of the user-interface once again was done with a console in mind but the control setup is easily accessible and comfortable to use across all platforms with quick customisation available just in case | the ui is less intrusive than previous tes games adopting more of a minimalistic aesthetic along with a rather beautiful screen for the character and perk trees | however navigating the base inventory system comes down to personal preference | the a | i has received notable improvements in combat particularly but still remains rather amusing when reacting to stealth and long-ranged attacks | as i'm sure i don't need to mention the legendary status of the obligatory 'bethesda bugs' the oblivious nature of a | i | during stealth will most likely remain a quirky charm for the developer though whether this detracts from immersion depends on how seriously you're invested into it | nope that arrow in your eye isn't your imagination | with the extraordinary detail that has gone into the world and thus to cater to a wider audience quests and factions overall are unfortunately hit-and-miss scenarios in terms of depth and enjoyment | while they're certainly keeping with the dark and gritty theme that the harsh life of skyrim presents there's admittedly an over-reliance on thinly-veiled fetch-quests and straight-forward dungeon crawls | the main quest unfortunately falls flat despite like most of the other major quests taking place in often quite striking and well-designed locations as the writing adopts a level of ambiguity and repetition that is so open it ultimately detracts from the player's immersion especially when as the saviour of the entire world you're being ordered about by some random npc | some factions are admittedly enjoyable but they also require a grind to truly get going in the first place and how rewarding a quest chain can be is dependent on the time put in | i still remember playing skyrim for the first time years back on the playstation and loving it initially sinking in as much time whenever i could | it's a bit hard to explain in retrospect but the reason why it was so successful was because it was unlike anything this type of community had ever seen with the new creation engine and potential that it presented everyone was caught up in the inevitable hype | naturally its popularity and sales was secured almost immediately and even people who had never played a video game or an rpg in general were immediate diehards | it was released to a fanfare of critical acclaim and much like doom and half-life before it became highly influential for its time and still remains a frequently cited benchmark for other games to compete with | as time went by however the more you played it the more it felt like something was missing that you weren't getting the full package | similar to a certain other game that was recently released the game world itself captured everyone's attention in the midst of rampant hype but reality caught up to show just how far bethesda needs to go to hit that balance of content and depth that can make their games so great | for everything that the elder scrolls v: skyrim gets right there is something to equally hold it back | it is not a 'bad game' per se and can certainly still be recommended to pretty much everyone due to how accessible it is but whether or not you'll love it comes down to your experience in other role-playing games and how much of its failings you're willing to endure | it is an admirable feat and it's easy to feel all the love and effort that bgs put into it but on the whole skyrim ultimately feels like a rough outline rather than the engrossing fantasy epic that the game was meant to be; a world that one almost seemed to have expected the modding community to finish for themselves | it simply doesn't feel as if your character matters or that you can even truly affect the world and while skyrim certainly presents an impressive framework for a role-playing game a lot of it simply isn't backed up | npc dialogue loops are especially forgettable | the vanilla experience is undeniably time-consuming and it has been and will continue to be thoroughly enjoyed by most people | but if you do wish to pick this up and you haven't already take the time to install mods to make skyrim into the game it should've been |

review_text: star wars: the force unleashed ii is the second instalment in the series | being developed by aspyr media and published by lucas arts taking place between the rd and th episodes of star wars | the game was released in october on pc xbox ps nintendo ds and the wii | the game continues the story of you playing starkiller a student of darth vadar | the gameplay is very much the same as the first game but we have some new additions to his force abilities such as mind tricks allowing you to mind control enemies to either fleeing the fight or fighting on your side | the second new element is the ability to use force fury; which is basically you enraged form that allows you to go crazy with lighting fast light sabre hits fancy flips and electric force shots and all sorts of craziness | the overall gameplay is essentially the same as the first game though | enemy fights throughout the level are very samey throughout your play through; with a few new enemies being added in which require a rock paper scissors way of thinking so only one of your abilities beat them whilst the rest of virtually no damage | the boss fights in unleashed ii are a bit of a let down apart from the final scenes | quick time events play a prominent part in any boss fight which is something i absolutely detest most of the time | it felt very cheap and showed a lack of innovation to force a key boss fight to be resolved by simply using quick time events | the only boss fight throughout the game that was anything at all compelling is the final fight with darth vader which is rather memorable in my opinion of being one of the better boss fights from the series so far | the graphics are sadly very drab too; the low-quality textures and poor quality models ruin the games aesthetic | the game does have a few redeeming factors in that the special effects from lightning and the light sabres do look really good though | the voice acting from the main characters just feel a little bit off; i couldnt quite put my finger on what was different but it just felt very poorly executed in the final cut | darth vadar and yoda have the best voice acting throughout but the main character starkiller just sounds so monotone that youd find it a challenge to stay awake listening to him for any extended amount of time | difficulty wise unleashed ii is easier than the first game; there are no challenging fights or platforming scenes you can ramp up the difficulty at the start of the play through but the lack of being able to change this on the fly once you have started is disappointing | like i said boss fights usually conclude in quick time events and regular enemy fights are nothing other than a time filler as they offer no challenge what-so-ever | i finished the game in just under four hours; which is similar to the time it took me to finish the first game so there has been no improvement made on the amount of content on offer | this was another huge disappointment for me as the story really could be explained and drawn out a little longer for the benefit of the player | you may be able to squeeze a second play throughout of this game but only if you didnt finish the game the first time round on hard mode | there is a selection of collectables to find throughout the story mode which allows you to customize your light sabres colours but there isnt really anything else other than that available | the game is also riddled with technical problems | the main one being the frame rate is capped at | this is an absolute disgrace even though it was six years ago dont cap frame rates | secondly is the huge amount of graphically tearing and no options are available for v-sync to fix it | i also had a number of crashes to desktop during my time playing too; these come just before you reach a save point on a level too which leaves you with the annoyance of having to replay the last checkpoint of the previous stage too | its also worth mentioning that i played the game completely using my controllers the mouse and keyboard support is lacking so i wouldnt even suggest trying them | sadly star wars: the force unleashed ii is a poor excuse for the second instalment in this series | the first game is a country mile better and being a fan of star wars i was hugely disappointed with the overall production values on offer here as well as an extremely short experience | the technical problems and repetitive nature of the gameplay does the game no favours either | this game is nowhere near worth the price of | and it should not be recommended for anyone but hardcore fans of star wars and even then it is with a huge caution | tom's score card stay away not recommended only recommended when on sale recommended highly recommended this is a must play if you found this review helpful please give it a thumbs up | if you would also like to follow my reviews more easily be sure to join my group by clicking here and checking out the teamtom review site [teamtomreviews | co | uk]

review_text: before i explain why i am recommending this game to you i will first offer the following disclaimers: do not buy this game at full price | you should feel comfortable with your purchase if it is between $ and $ | while others are reporting performance issues and crashes i have not experienced this at all | beyond running the executive file in windows xp service pack compatibility mode i have done no further tweaking to get the game to run on windows | i am running the game at x with all graphics settings set to high | while the game does run at fps i have not experienced any dips in fps or anything of this nature | i expect the stability of the game in my experience to be due to my specs gpu: nvidia gtx ti cpu: intel core i-k and gb ram | the game is very short | if you were to only play through the campaign once you would get roughly four to five hours of play | there is a challenge mode offered which can be a handy way to test out your abilities and skill in a variety of game modes ranging from merely practicing combos in a timed environment to timed wave based elimination modes | the game offers two distinct endings and four difficulty settings so your mileage will depend on whether you are a completionist or just out for a short but sweet star wars experience | so given the above disclaimers why am i recommending this game to you | the simple answer is because i found the game to be a short yet enjoyable star wars experience | while the game does nothing ground breaking it doesn't have the most varied combat and enemies can be bland and uninspiring at times this game does do a number of things right that make up for these flaws | first it captures the 'look and feel' of the star wars universe | the graphics do an admirable job of capturing the style of the movies and although others have criticised them i personally think they are perfectly adequate and at times quite beautiful | not ground breaking but sufficiently emersing | in particular i really enjoyed the character design for starkiller | some of the costumes you unlock throughout the game can only be described as design porn | the repurposed tie fighter uniform provides a memorable example | while there is nothing particularly deep about starkiller's character i enjoyed listening to sam witwer's voice acting and found him to be interesting enough to carry the story from start to finish | although there appears to be very little to his character development beyond chasing after a love interest and questioning his origins | second the combat is fun enough that you will likely enjoy the four to five hour journey to the story's conclusion | the game tries to switch up enemies although for the most part you will be fighting familiar enemies and watching the same kill animations for the mini-bosses you will fight on the way | the bosses themselves can be challenging at times but not so difficult that you want to put the game and never return | they also offer some variety to the combat and often require you to use your force abilities and skills to successfully overcome your foes | it should be stressed that there is some handholding in the boss sections and generous checkpoints that refill your health but not the enemies detracts from the difficulty | third using some of the force powers really recaptured the feeling of playing jedi academy as a child | in particular the force grab skill can be a lot of fun to use and play around with and brings back a lot of fond memories of levelling up force chock in academy and sadistically toying with the stormtroopers | the force powers you are provided and the games use of them does do a good job of making you feel like a complete badass and a powerful force user | for these reasons i enjoyed the force unleashed ii and would recommend the game to others | i want to give an extra special mention to that tie fighter uniform again because it is seriously cool | so in summation: the game is short so only purchase it when it is on sale | while it won't be the best star wars game you have played or third person action game for that matter it will be enjoyable while it lasts | in my humble opinion it does a good job of capturing the spirit of the star wars universe and this feeling lasts for the entirety of the campaign | the combat finds a middle ground between fun and uninspired but i is still enjoyed it for the length of the game | if you want to play a star wars game for a couple of hours and feel like a powerful jedi then this game is worth a purchase | i would explore jedi academy first but this game is certainly worth a try |

review_text: so i've played all of the arkham games and i must say half of the game is just so disappointing and the other half is really good and a great improvement from the past games | pros: has the same arkham feel and formula but it improves and adds upon it: everything feels % exactly the same which is a good thing mind you | the combat the flying the skill tree the gadgets | all is there all controls and feels the same etc | there's some new gadgets not a lot and none too interesting but still additions nonetheless | you can grapnel boost higher smash through windows throw batarangs mid-flight and most importantly there's many more moves and combos you can pull off | if you can master all the different moves and combos you can pull off some really stylish looking hits which makes playing as batman feel even more badass and even more like batman | the animations are also very smooth most of the time | yes batman can still magically roll feet within a second to punch another enemy but most of the time every counter ever double takedown hell even triple takedowns look so natural and seamlessly happen during combat | graphics: i usually don't factor graphics into my opinion on a game but the graphics in this game are so insane that i'd actually consider it a selling point | the rains effects are really good | the way you can see each individual drop hit your head and your cape the way it looks on the ground and the way it hits the side of building looks really really good | the shaders the lighting and the level of detail on every character is just insane | and don't even get me started on the water | just look at the ocean | the waves are huge and move so realistically | best looking water in a game ever and yes i'd say this is the second best looking game unmodded next to battlefront ever | gotham city is x times larger: the map is much bigger | gotham city is finally of respectable size | it could've had maybe one more island in there to really seal the deal but it's still a major improvement over city | arkham city was too small and felt 'bordered' if you get me | blackgate being in the center ruined it because it just created an invisible wall that ruined traversal | it just felt very claustrophobic all the buildings were short there wasn't anything to see and the buildings were too densely packed | this however has three and a half islands all well sized spread openly with no obstructions besides neighboring buildings and most importantly has a lot of iconic batman landmarks like falcone shipping wayne tower ace chemicals lex corp etc | these said buildings are really high which makes gotham city feel like a proper gotham city | now onto the negatives of the game | cons: long drawn out and terrible story: the story is the same crap | most of gotham has conveniently evacuated big bad villains have taken over yata yata | that's all fine and dandy i guess but just pointing out that it's nothing original | as far as it being drawn out well it is | it goes on for about hours which is too long in my opinion | especially considering there's a fair amount of filler in the story more on this later | basically the arkham knight is some 'new' not really 'mysterious' not really villain who knows who batman is and wants to kill him | not gonna spoil who he is but it's very easy to tell who he is if you've read the comics especially death in the family which is not canon to arkham knight but similar backstories with a certain someone | not trying to spoil it if i can help it | batmobile is overused to the point where it's almost a joke: in my opinion the overuse of the batmobile does not make the game unplayable like people say nor is it as overused as you might think but it is still very overused | just not every other mission or anything like that to add to my disclaimer it is overused way too much | it's an awesome and welcomed addition to the arkham games but i feel like doubling it up as a tank ruined the game too much | there are way too many moments where batman or a civilian is stuck in a rut and the batmobile acts as a deus ex machina to save the day | getting shot by tanks | have no fear batmobile is here | here's some mindless tank battles with unmanned tanks | need to get past an obstruction | have no fear batmobile is here | here's a tow cable that will conveniently tear the wall down or solve some puzzle | it feels like the game is parodying itself | i find it hilarious | also the deathstroke boss fight is a god damn tank battle | i have to spoil this because you can't get your hopes up for a boss fight against one of the coolest batman villains unfortunately | shame because the deathstroke boss fight in origins was the best boss fight in any of the arkham games | overall the tank battles are filler and copouts for actual well designed boss fights | side quests take the ubisoft route: what i mean by this is they took the lazy route to the side quests and just copy and pasted the same exact objective for each side quest times over | there's those farcry inspired outposts which are poorly designed for both predator and open fights more filler cannon fodder tank battles to engage in to clean up gotham etc | even the side quests with actual villains are the same thing | for the firefly missions all you do is put out a fire chase firefly take him down and he gets away | same exact thing for man bat | see him flying go after him take him down inject him with whatever and he flies away | i know the side quests in arkham city were all the same formular to a degree but this is just more of that lazy game design in this game | they somehow managed to make the joker return and it feels so ham fisted: don't get me wrong i love the joker i think mark hamill does a great job voice acting him this game included but it's poorly executed and very intrusive to the main story | it's poorly executed because he shows up around every corner | even during important moments that have nothing to do with him | he just never shuts up it's distracting and while he's well voice acted like i said rocksteady have found a way to make me despise him | might be because he's in all four of the arkham games | maybe some verbal interaction between batman and joker would've been nice but no | he's just there and batman is a mute | if batman talked to him this could've given them the opportunity to at least give a little exposition on the arkhamverse lore | joker was great in asylum and city but he died at the end of city | we need to move on from him now | arkham knight is poorly voice acted: despite being voiced by troy baker he just sounds like some hacker nerd with an inferiority complex | i liked the way he was voiced during the scene where batman reveals the arkham knight's identity but that's just one several minute long cutscene | conclusion: all in all i think it's pretty good | many improvements but also there are some major things that ruin the game | it had the potential to be the best arkham game but it failed | i will still recommend it because it's a nice improvement from the previous games and it's not bad to the point where an arkham fan should skip playing it | it is definitely worth getting in | it's $ | now $ | if you can get it on sale | you will get your money's worth | as far as optimization is concerned it's definitely gotten better but there's still stutters and wonky framerate fluctuations | this sounds very damage controlling of me to say but it looks better than the ps version so it's fine in my opinion especially considering the amazing graphics and the low price | strong definitely buy if you love the arkham games and need your batman fix but it's a letdown nonetheless | cheap price should make it a little more acceptable |

underwhelming villain i've ever seen in a game and even ignoring his awful surfer bro voice all he ever really does is brag about knowing everything about you and then immediately start whining and throwing an almost riddler-level crybaby tantrum whenever you start getting the upper hand making him seem more like a spoiled child than a villain worth putting in the title | he just isn't an review_text: purely a review of the game itself: to fully understand the batman: arkham franchise you must first understand that most of the batman games prior to that were either terrible in the case of batman forever or completely off-the-wall insane as in batman: return of the joker's strange contra-esque gameplay | about the only game prior to arkham asylum to capture the essence of the series would have been batman: the animated series game on the snes but even that only aped the visual style and missed the boat on the crime-solving detective aspects | arkham asylum was the first game that really let you feel like you were stepping into batman's shoes | from using the shadows and verticality as your allies to take enemies down stealthily to using the environment gadgets and good old-fashioned brainpower arkham asylum and arkham city delivered both content and the batman 'feel' with verve and panache | full disclosure; i never finished arkham origins because i felt like it took an interesting concept and threw it down the drain to cram the joker in yet again as the prime villain | i'm pleased to report that with rocksteady's final batman game arkham knight the style and quality of the story have returned in spades | many moons and many dollars during pre-production marketing were spent on building the mystery of the arkham knight one of the game's major antagonists | if you are versed with batman lore you'll probably figure it out a quarter of the way through the game if it hasn't been spoiled for you already | even if you can see the twist from a mile away some of the returning voice actors from the animated series coupled with an above-average script handle the material beautifully and it's a joy to be a part of the story | the game strikes a masterful balance between gameplay and story capably delivering relevant material to you in sidequests radio chatter and batman's dialogues with the various characters | even if they do throw a lot of story material at you overall it never feels truly overwhelming and due to the game's impressive length it doesn't feel cramped | from a gameplay perspective there's certainly a lot to do and while most of it falls into a number of broad categories the sidequest stories themselves and the situations keep the game's many missions feeling fresh | you'll solve tons of the riddler's puzzles rescue firemen discover an arsonist's plot train azrael clear the skies and the roads of the arkham knight's automated army all of which are only a portion of the things you'll do during your time with the game | i will say that they are very proud of their batmobile content as it is utilized in almost every plotline in the game in some fashion or another | some like it some hate it; i found that it controls well enough that it never really felt like a chore to use although soaring through the skies on batman's space-age glidey wings never gets old and just feels right | another thing that feels right is the combat | arkham origins' combat felt stilted while arkham knight's is smooth and makes you feel powerful | as you progress through the game's skill and tech trees unlocking various cool takedowns and methods of mayhem to unleash on unsuspecting and suspecting thugs the game rolls out new enemy types and configurations to test your prowess | there's never a dull moment | another thing that i feel deserves a mention is the quality of gotham itself; it feels much more alive than in either city or origins | while the city is locked down due to martial law and the invasion of the arkham knight's forces there are riots occurring all over and the rainy grimy neon feel of gotham is in full effect | from the aging facades of chinatown to the hyper-modern glass monoliths on the upscale founder's island this vision of gotham is breathtaking no matter where you look | purely a review of the port: godawful | unstable as hell highly variable performance across different builds for no discernible reason fps lock missing graphical effects incredibly delayed fix that actually broke it even more on my machine etc etc | this is precisely how not to roll a game out onto the pc | luckily i was able to beat the game before they broke it even further and now we're looking at the end of october to potentially fix it | absolutely ridiculous and shameful |

review_text: when i played arkham origins i thought it was a fine game with some notable flaws that made it inferior to arkham city but all would be made right with the release of arkham knight | but that's not exactly what happened instead i think arkham knight is a fine game with some notable flaws that make it inferior to arkham city | let's tackle the first elephant in the room: the botched port and initial release | it stank up steam so bad that it single-handedly kickstarted popularized the refund policy thanks to link xl for pointing out refunds actually started a bit earlier than ak and it was the reason i held off on actually buying it until a good long while had passed despite being a massive fan of the series | i can be brief about this: my brand new rig has gb of memory and a gtx and the game runs at a near-constant fps at p maxed settings while looking absolutely gorgeous | now i get that not everyone has had that experience or will have that experience but i can only judge the game on how it plays for me at this point in time and i have no reason to complain | that's not to say i tihnk that putting out a release as broken as this one is in any way acceptable or excusable it's not but i'm not going to count it against the game in its current state | the same can't be said for elephant number two which is the batmobile | the dynamic duo in this game isn't batman and robin but batman and his amazing rooftop-hopping car | it quickly veers from cool into silly and contrived and about the only thing missing is the batmobile doing inverted takedowns it does hang upside down a few times so that's not as implausible as it sounds | they made sure you can't miss out on the experience by putting in vehicular combat and puzzles that require the batmobile but i found myself more frustrated than entertained by these sections | despite what the game designers thought it would have been completely fine if the batmobile had just been there as a cooler way of getting you from a to b | throw in the optional racetracks for the people who like that sort of thing i'm fine with that | have maybe one sequence where the batmobile gets to slug it out with a tank or helicopter sure | but repeated vehicular combat sequences and painfully forced puzzle sequences just detract from the experience | while you can avoid almost all racing and puzzles if you just don't go after the riddler as if | the tank battles are there to stay | it's as if someone baked you a delicious velvety smooth chocolate cake except that they mixed in crunchy peanuts to chip your teeth on because they read somewhere that chocolate and peanuts go well together | there are a lot of things arkham knight gets right too | the meat and potatoes of the game combat and predator encounters work as smooth as ever and there are the requisite tweaks and new moves to keep things interesting without completely unbalancing things like the shock gloves in origins did | there's a smorgasbord of villains on the loose in gotham waiting for you to arrest them and they all involve different gameplay so you can easily mix things up without getting bored | the voice acting is top notch both from the regulars and the guest villains special tip of the hat to dwight schultz who plays a terrifying professor pyg i was surprised to find out it was him when i looked it up | the story is engaging and i'm happy to say that's still the case even if you had the identity of the arkham knight spoiled before you picked up the game like i did | i especially like the way the writers justified the issue of batman suddenly deciding to stick massive guns on his batmobile even if they do conveniently fire 'non-lethal rounds' when targeting humans | if this sounds a bit out of character for batman it's because it is | and you'll find out why as you play the game | having said that i'm definitely not a fan of the ending the true ending you get with % completion which is deliberately ambiguous on the ultimate fate of batman and gotham | it's not terrible i can live with it but it still feels like a cop-out and something the writers could absolutely have avoided in favor of a stronger statement | as a cap to the whole series it's a bit underwhelming | arkham knight gets an easy 'recommended' from me but it's not as great as the final installment could have been review_text: the core of the game is unchanged from previous versions: you are batman you fight mooks and members of the batfamily rogues gallery | you use the freeflow combat system to attack dodge and counter you sneak up on thugs and scare the crap out of them | odds are very good that if you enjoyed the previous arkham titles you'll like this one | batman: arkham knight does have technical problems | textures can be slow to load frame rate can experience sudden drops and chug for several seconds the camera can swerve or focus on something i didn't intend and screw a jump or grappel enough to make me groan | it does crash | i have fifty hours in and have experienced four crashes | three when entering the batmobile one when loading a new level and i received a steam chat message | all of the crashes were related to graphical issues | it also has mechanical problems | the batmobile as often as it is featured and as much as it is required adds little to the game | it's clumsy to drive and while it is faster than gliding i found it to be much less desirable to do | fights against drones are shallow and lack the natural complexity of the still excellent freeflow system | are there more challenges to come | i hope so | i love replaying the challenges for better times and higher scores | i also enjoy fighting thugs as nightwing | there are fewer character challenges than there are batmobile challenges which disappoints me | i want more time as the crime fighters not their stuff | but all of this aside batman: arkham knight has done something few games are capable doing and that is showing us the rise and fall of a character | tell a full story a full trilogy with a prequel tie in | the series is not well known for its dialogue but it should be lauded for its storytelling | they deal with raw themes and motifs good versus evil light and darkness monsters but the characters and setting drip with that sort of unfiltered emotion and presence | it's very rich | replaying the main game is as fluid as the combat system because of how seamless events transition and how simple it is to skip cinematics you'd rather not see | if you're not sure about this one wait | get it on special and then play it | buy at the price point you're comfortable with and i'm confident you'll enjoy it | edit: i've replayed batman arkham asylum and batman: arkham origins since writing this review | both games as excellent as they are have similar performance issues on my machine | i experienced two crashes in origins three in asylum | regardless i enjoyed my replays as much as i enjoyed this game |
